item.title: Science Cafe — Wed Nov 11, 5:30 PM — ca
item.description:
G STREET WUNDERBAR. Hosted by Prof. Jared Shaw, featuring expert speakers on a variety of topics! Brought to you by the UCD College of Letters & Science. 5:30p—7:30p. Free
The Davis Science Café series was founded in 2012 by Professor Jared Shaw, initially supported by the National Science Foundation and currently supported by the College of Letters and Science and promoted by Capital Science Communicators. Over the years, the #DavisSciCafe has been held at the Arboretum, Crepeville, de Vere’s, and most recently has settled in at G Street WunderBar. Café topics have spanned the likes of milk science, wine science, sea level rise, hyperdimensional geometry, and coral reef ecology. So come on by, and let’s drink to science! Hosted on the second Wednesday of each month. Free to the public.
Location: G Street Wunderbar Date: Hosted on the second Wednesday of each month Time: 5:30 – 6:30 pm
Source: The Dirt

item.title: ASUCD Housing Fair — Thu Nov 12, 10:00 AM
item.description:
The biannual ASUCD Housing Fair is next scheduled for Thursday, November 12, 2026 on the Quad. It is hosted by UC Davis ASUCD's own Housing Advising Undergraduate Students (HAUS) and run in partnership with CollegePads (https://www.rentcollegepads.com/).
The event is for students, by students, and is FREE! Come and one-stop-shop the best places to live in Davis for the coming year. All are welcome including undergraduates, graduate/professional students as well as members of the public.
At every Housing Fair, we host over 50 apartment complex managers and resource representatives. This staff helps answer your pressing questions as well as make sure you find a place that is aligned with your needs and wants. Housing Fair is filled not only with an array of information, but with swag and prizes! We hope to see you at our next Fair!

item.title: Author Talk: S. E. Wendel — Tue Nov 10, 6:30 PM — The Avid Reader Bookstore
item.description: Celebrate the release of local author, S. E. Wendel’s new book, Heartsworn. She will be joined in conversation by Angela Montoya. About the Book Return to the world of Heartsong! A reclusive researcher gets the shock of a lifetime when the (very attractive) gargoyle statue in her rose garden awakens and claims her as his mate. She’s known him all her life… June Parkhurst is a prodigy, a conservator, and…an empath. Yet, her empathic abilities don’t feel like a gift; they’re a curse, one that’s driven her into isolation. Overwhelmed by the feelings of others and her own grief, June sticks to what she loves most: statues. She’s always been fascinated by them, especially the gothic masterpiece in her family’s rose garden. He’s watched over her for years… For centuries, Alaric has despaired. Cursed to stone by the cruel Faerie Queen, Alaric has watched the world pass him by. He holds desperately onto a fleeting hope—that one day, June will come to understand what he’s known for years

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Wed Nov 11, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Nov 11, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p

item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Jan 27, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:

item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
